notes: One shared 4096-byte allocation read by two tasks: counted once. The figures below are the whole published certificate, not a chosen subset — the runner rebuilds the map from the certificate and compares it wholesale, so a changed union rule moves a pinned number. epoch_peak = union 4096 + summed private peaks (1024 + 1024) + overhead (512 + 2*128) = 6912. The route is check-only: no emitted C, no reference execution, no native run.

controls.note: Two distinct 4096-byte cells, each read by both tasks, are two footprints: the union is 8192 and the epoch peak rises by exactly that 4096. The union counts cell identities, not readers, which is the claim CT35 makes; only shared_entry_union, epoch_peak, completed_residency and exit_residency move.

One task naming the same cell twice is refused at Q630 DuplicateSharedEntry, not silently deduplicated. Without this control, counting-once could be an artifact of a lowering that collapses repeats rather than a checked rule.
